what_it_does: Forms an occlusive layer that helps reduce water loss and soften dry skin.
summary_short: Mineral oil is a classic occlusive moisturizer: it helps trap water in the skin and smooth rough, dry areas. Cosmetic-grade mineral oil is highly refined and generally considered low-irritation, though it can feel heavy or greasy for some users.
summary_long:
Mineral oil is a purified, petroleum-derived emollient and occlusive. In skincare, its main job is to sit on top of the skin and slow transepidermal water loss, which helps skin stay hydrated and feel softer. It does not “add” water on its own, so it works best when layered over water-based humectants or used in formulas that already contain them.

Its benefits are most noticeable for dry, compromised, or barrier-stressed skin. Mineral oil is commonly used in creams, ointments, cleansing oils, baby products, and makeup removers because it is stable, inexpensive, and unlikely to oxidize compared with many plant oils.

Cosmetic-grade mineral oil is highly refined, and the safety concerns sometimes associated with crude petroleum do not apply in the same way to properly purified skincare ingredients. It is generally considered low-allergen and low-irritation, which is why it appears in many products for sensitive or very dry skin.

For acne-prone users, mineral oil is often less comedogenic than its reputation suggests, but the finished formula matters. Heavy ointments or rich creams containing mineral oil may feel too occlusive for oily skin or may worsen breakouts for some individuals, especially if paired with richer waxes or comedogenic esters.

Mineral oil pairs well with humectants like glycerin, hyaluronic acid, urea, and panthenol, plus barrier-supporting ingredients like petrolatum, ceramides, and fatty alcohols. There are no major ingredient conflicts, but it can reduce the elegant feel of lightweight formulas if used at high levels.
quick_facts: Best for dry or barrier-stressed skin
Low allergy potential for most users
Can feel heavy on oily skin
